title: The US is about to tell 35 countries to choose between it and China on AI
excerpt: A draft US letter warns the 35 Pax Silica and AI Opportunity Statement signatories they cannot also join China's rival AI framework.
content_html:
Michael Martina reported the draft for Reuters on 14 August, citing a US official and an internal document. The letter goes to the 35 signatories of an American “AI Opportunity Statement” from June. Its message is that countries must choose.

The wording is blunt for a diplomatic text. “To be part of everything is to be part of nothing,” it says. Signing the Pax Silica Declaration is “not merely a membership subscription, but a commitment”. The letter urges countries to choose deliberately.

Reuters could not establish when Washington will send it, or whether the text changes first. The draft is undated. The State Department said it would not comment on “purportedly leaked internal documents”.

What Pax Silica actually is

Washington launched it last year. The aim is to secure supply chains across three things at once: AI models, semiconductors and critical minerals.

About two dozen countries have joined. Reuters names Japan, Australia, South Korea and Kazakhstan. Members get access to shared investment opportunities in AI projects, and the framework pushes them towards joint projects and coordinated export controls.

The wider group is looser. Signing the AI Opportunity Statement means agreeing symbolically on a “common purpose” and a “shared vision” with the US, according to the State Department’s own posting. That is the group of 35 now receiving the letter.

The framework is non-binding. That is precisely the gap the letter is trying to close.

One country set this off

Kazakhstan joined Pax Silica in June. The State Department made a point of it at the time, with Under Secretary Jacob Helberg marking it as the first Central Asian accession. The country holds significant reserves of the minerals that advanced chips depend on.

It then joined China’s framework as well. Kazakhstan is the only country known to have signed up to both, and Reuters reports that this set off alarm bells in Washington.

The minerals are what make it awkward. China has already used its near-monopolies here as a retaliatory weapon during the tariff war. A supplier hedging between the two blocs is the exact scenario Pax Silica exists to prevent.

What Xi launched in July

The rival body is barely a month old. Xi Jinping announced a World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization at a Shanghai conference, and pitched China’s open-weight models as the alternative to American influence.

The offer is different in kind. Pax Silica offers investment access and shared controls. Beijing offers models you can download.

China’s own position is less open than the pitch suggests. Reuters reported in July that Beijing is weighing restrictions on overseas access to its leading models. Both sides are working out how much access they are willing to give away.

The word the letter avoids

China is not mentioned. The letter refers instead to “duplicative initiatives whose expectations conflict with our own”, and leaves the reader to fill in the name.

The US official Reuters spoke to was less careful. Officials drafted it to make clear “you can’t have it both ways”, the official said, on condition of anonymity.

The rest of that quote is the argument in full. It is difficult to see how a country can credibly position itself as a trusted partner in one technology ecosystem, the official said. Not while it signs up to an initiative designed by China to advance a competing vision.

The timing is not accidental

Chinese open-weight models have closed much of the gap on the proprietary systems from OpenAI and Anthropic. Hugging Face’s chief executive put numbers on it this month, telling CNBC that China is winning the open-model race with 41% of downloads.

American industry is not united behind the closed approach either. Nvidia and several other large firms broke with OpenAI and Anthropic over open weights this year.

The enforcement machinery has been tightening in parallel. The Commerce Department is examining how China gets remote access to Nvidia chips it cannot buy. The Treasury Secretary has threatened to sanction Chinese AI firms outright.

Europe does not appear in this story

Here is what stands out from a European desk. Reuters names Japan, Australia, South Korea and Kazakhstan among the members. It names no European country at all.

That is not proof of absence, because the report does not publish the full list. It is still striking for a framework covering chips and critical minerals, given how much of both Europe handles.

Brussels has spent the year building a third position rather than picking a side. The Made in EU rules start at a 5% local-content threshold and cover hardware, and the sovereignty push runs through European compute, European satellites and European models.

A letter demanding a binary choice arrives into that. Whether any European capital receives one is the thing to watch.

The counter-argument arrived within hours

The China analyst Rui Ma made the case that the letter may cost more than it gains. Writing on X, she argued that the world is watching one side weaponise supply chains and controlled access. The other promotes open technology and broad access.

Her point about durability is the sharper one. Alliances are not permanent and incentives change, she wrote, which is a caution about coercion rather than a defence of Beijing.

A third argument turned up alongside it. Several developers responded that countries should build their own systems and depend on neither bloc, because either dependency hands someone else a switch over your economy. That is easier to say than to fund.

What would settle it

Three things, and the first is whether the letter is ever sent. It is a draft, it is undated, and the State Department has not confirmed it exists.

The second is Kazakhstan. It is the test case, it holds the minerals, and what it does when the letter lands tells you whether the threat has force.

The third is the full membership list. Pax Silica has announced accessions one at a time. Until the 35 names surface, nobody outside Washington can say whom the US is asking to choose.

content_html_zh:
迈克尔·马丁纳 (Michael Martina) 8 月 14 日援引一名美国官员和一份内部文件为路透社报道了这份草案。 这封信是写给 6 月份美国《人工智能机会声明》的 35 个签署者的。 它传达的信息是各国必须做出选择。

对于外交文本来说，措辞显得生硬。 它说：“成为一切的一部分就等于什么都不是。” 签署 Pax Silica 宣言“不仅仅是会员资格，更是一种承诺”。 这封信敦促各国慎重选择。

路透社无法确定华盛顿何时发送该消息，也无法确定文本是否会首先发生变化。 该草案未注明日期。 美国国务院表示不会对“据称泄露的内部文件”发表评论。

Pax Silica 到底是什么

华盛顿去年启动了它。 其目标是同时确保三项供应链的安全：人工智能模型、半导体和关键矿物。

大约有二十几个国家加入了。 路透社点名日本、澳大利亚、韩国和哈萨克斯坦。 成员可以获得人工智能项目的共享投资机会，该框架推动他们开展联合项目和协调出口管制。

群体越广泛，就越松散。 根据国务院自己的帖子，签署人工智能机会声明意味着象征性地与美国就“共同目标”和“共同愿景”达成一致。 现在收到这封信的有 35 人。

该框架不具有约束力。 这正是这封信试图弥合的差距。

一个国家引发了这一事件

哈萨克斯坦于 6 月加入 Pax Silica。 美国国务院当时特别强调了这一点，副国务卿雅各布·赫尔伯格将其标记为第一个中亚国家加入。 该国拥有先进芯片所依赖的大量矿产资源。

随后它也加入了中国的框架。 哈萨克斯坦是已知唯一签署了这两项协议的国家，路透社报道称，这在华盛顿敲响了警钟。

矿物质让它变得尴尬。 中国已经在关税战期间利用其近乎垄断的地位作为报复武器。 两个集团之间的供应商对冲正是 Pax Silica 所要防止的情况。

习近平七月推出了什么

对手的身体才成立不到一个月。 习近平在上海会议上宣布成立世界人工智能合作组织，并将中国的开放重量模式作为美国影响力的替代方案。

报价的种类不同。 Pax Silica 提供投资访问和共享控制。 北京提供模型可供下载。

中国自己的立场并不像宣传中所暗示的那么开放。 路透社 7 月份报道称，北京正在考虑限制海外市场获取其领先车型。 双方正在研究愿意放弃多少访问权限。

这封信避免使用的词

没有提到中国。 这封信提到了“重复的举措，其期望与我们自己的期望相冲突”，并让读者填写名称。

路透社采访的美国官员则没那么谨慎。 这位不愿透露姓名的官员表示，官员们起草这份文件是为了明确“两者不能兼得”。

该引文的其余部分是完整的论点。 这位官员表示，很难看出一个国家如何才能将自己可靠地定位为一个技术生态系统中值得信赖的合作伙伴。 当它签署了一项由中国设计的旨在推进竞争愿景的倡议时，情况就不同了。

时机并非偶然

中国的开放权重模型已经缩小了与 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 专有系统的大部分差距。 Hugging Face 首席执行官本月公布了数据，他告诉 CNBC，中国以 41% 的下载量赢得了开放模型竞赛。

美国工业界也没有团结起来支持封闭的做法。 Nvidia 和其他几家大公司今年在开放权重问题上与 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 决裂。

执法机制也在同时收紧。 美国商务部正在研究中国如何远程访问它无法购买的英伟达芯片。 美国财政部长威胁要彻底制裁中国人工智能公司。

欧洲没有出现在这个故事中

这是欧洲办公桌的突出之处。 路透社将日本、澳大利亚、韩国和哈萨克斯坦列为其成员。 它根本没有提到任何欧洲国家。

这并不能证明缺席，因为该报告没有公布完整名单。 考虑到欧洲处理的木片和关键矿物的数量，这个涵盖木片和关键矿物的框架仍然令人震惊。

布鲁塞尔这一年一直在打造第三个位置，而不是选边站。 欧盟制造规则以 5% 的本地含量门槛为起点，涵盖硬件，而主权推动则贯穿欧洲计算、欧洲卫星和欧洲模型。

一封要求二元选择的信到达了那里。 欧洲各国首都是否会收到这一信号值得关注。

反驳意见在数小时内到达

中国分析师马睿认为，这封信的代价可能大于其收益。 她在《X》上撰文指出，世界正在关注一方将供应链和受控访问武器化。 另一个促进开放技术和广泛的访问。

她关于耐用性的观点更为尖锐。 她写道，联盟不是永久性的，激励措施也会发生变化，这是对胁迫的警告，而不是对北京的辩护。

与此同时，第三个论点也随之出现。 一些开发者回应说，各国应该建立自己的系统，并且不依赖任何一个集团，因为任何一个依赖都会让别人改变你的经济。 这说起来比资助容易。

什么可以解决它

三件事，第一是这封信是否寄出。 这是一份草案，没有注明日期，国务院也没有确认它的存在。

第二个是哈萨克斯坦。 这是测试用例，它包含矿物质，当信件到达时它会做什么，告诉你威胁是否具有威力。

三是完整的会员名单。 Pax Silica 一次宣布了一项加入。 在 35 名候选人浮出水面之前，华盛顿以外的任何人都无法说出美国要求选择谁。
